analysis.title: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) Q3'26 Review: Strong Operating Momentum Across All Segments, SI Compute & Monetization Drive Another Quarter of Positive Estimate Revisions
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on SPCX and raises its 12-month price target to $245 from $230 to reflect updated operating estimates after the Q3'26 report. With the stock at $147.79, GS shows 65.8% upside on the cover.
Q3'26 revenue and GAAP EBIT came in ahead of Street estimates, driven by AI segment revenue from cloud service agreements and continued Starlink adoption in both Consumer and Enterprise & Government.

Super Intelligence (SI) generated $7.6bn of Q3 revenue on 1.7GW of quarter-ending compute. Management guided to roughly 2.5-3GW by YE26 and another 10GW+ in 2027, with an upside case of more than 20GW by YE27.
Management said new compute at current pricing pays back in under 1 year. Comments on the call imply lower build costs and higher monetization could cut payback to about 6 months in 2027.

Compute demand is described as well ahead of supply. Short-duration contracts are renewing at higher $/watt, and management sees room to rent its compute several times over. Internal vs external use is expected to be about 50/50, with Grok Bot potentially the largest internal consumer.

Infrastructure, not chips, is the next constraint. Management named power, cooling and electrical infrastructure as the main bottlenecks and is targeting capacity for 20GW of incremental compute during 2027. Q4 capex alone is expected at $35-40bn, funded by operating cash flow, investment-grade debt access and possible value-chain partnerships.
Q1'27 revenue guidance of $33-37bn came in well ahead of GS and Street estimates and implies solid sequential growth. Management's December ARR target is $100bn.

Negatives in the quarter: Q4'26 capex guidance exceeded GS and Street estimates, and GAAP SI EBIT missed GS and Street estimates because of elevated stock-based compensation tied to the Cursor acquisition. Q3 SI GAAP EBIT was $431mm against GS $2,736mm and consensus $777mm.

GS expects heavy capital intensity across 2H26 and 2027 to leave future funding needs as an overhang on the stock until there is visibility on capital raises. GS assumes the raises are primarily debt.

Starship is the core economic enabler. Management targets weekly launches in 1H27 and about twice-weekly by end of 2027. Flight 15 aims to capture both booster and ship. Starlink v3 satellites plus Starship are framed as a path to 100x current constellation bandwidth over three years.

Connectivity is supported by Starlink Broadband today, with a larger long-term opportunity in Starlink Mobile after spectrum purchases. Management indicated an investor teach-in on mobility, held away from an earnings report, could be forthcoming.
SPCX and TSLA have each formed special committees of independent directors to discuss a potential business combination. GS gives no opinion on its likelihood or merits.

Estimate changes: Q4'26 GAAP EBIT cut to $4.71bn from $10.27bn and EPS to $0.44 from $1.02. FY27 revenue raised to $192.49bn from $127.46bn, EBIT to $79.16bn from $53.13bn, EPS to $5.52 from $3.96. FY28 EPS rises to $7.97 from $7.01.

The $245 target uses a sum-of-the-parts on 2029E segment estimates, discounted 1.25 years at 12%. Multiples are 9.5x EV/Sales for Space, 20.0x EV/EBIT for Connectivity (from 24.0x) and 25.0x EV/EBIT for SI (from 28.0x). GS cut the absolute multiples but raised SI's growth-adjusted multiple to 0.65x from 0.53x on better compute visibility.

GS lists near-term stock drivers as Starship launch data, Starlink broadband user growth and mobility build plans, compute scaling with strong monetization (Cursor, Grok, GrokBot), and flows from lock-up expirations. The shares are still about 25% below the post-IPO peak close.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated, PT raised from $230 to $245 on higher FY27-28 estimates and better SI compute visibility. GS sees a positive risk/reward skew with the shares about 25% below the post-IPO peak.

earnings_insights: SPCX Q3'26 reported revenue $14,575mm vs Visible Alpha consensus $12,809mm (+14%) and GS estimate $15,190mm (-4%).
SPCX Q3'26 reported GAAP EBIT $2,791mm vs consensus $2,356mm and GS estimate $4,667mm. Adjusted EBITDA $8,809mm vs consensus $6,837mm and GS $9,163mm.
SPCX Q3'26 reported GAAP EPS $0.35 vs consensus $0.16 and GS estimate $0.43. Reported free cash flow was -$9,805mm vs consensus -$11,627mm and GS -$2,929mm.
Q3'26 reported segment revenue: Space $1,767mm (consensus $1,458mm), Connectivity $5,248mm (consensus $4,917mm), Super Intelligence $7,560mm (consensus $6,435mm, GS $8,262mm).
Q3'26 reported segment GAAP EBIT: Connectivity $2,367mm vs consensus $1,870mm, SI $431mm vs consensus $777mm and GS $2,736mm, Space -$7mm vs consensus -$291mm.
Management guidance: Q1'27 revenue $33-37bn, above GS and Street. Q4'26 capex $35-40bn, above GS and Street.

GS estimate changes (GAAP): Q4'26E revenue $23.97bn (from $23.93bn), EBIT $4.71bn (from $10.27bn), EPS $0.44 (from $1.02). FY26E revenue $51.06bn, EBIT $5.41bn, EPS $0.50 (from $1.30). FY27E revenue $192.49bn, EPS $5.52. FY28E revenue $303.12bn, EPS $7.97.
GS FY27E free cash flow is -$172.0bn (from -$136.1bn) and FY26E is -$55.5bn (from -$29.5bn), reflecting the capex ramp.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SPCX shares, 12-month price target $245 from $147.79 (rating Buy since Jul 7, 2026)
trade_ideas.rationale: Scaling SI compute with sub-1-year payback, Starlink momentum and Starship cadence support estimate increases and a positive risk/reward skew.
trade_ideas.risk: Funding needs from high capital intensity, lock-up expirations, Starship reuse not proven, governance concentration in the founder and CEO.

risk_factors: Governance: majority voting power and execution risk concentrated in the Founder & CEO.
Related-party transactions with companies tied to the Founder & CEO, such as co-development of Terafab and Macrohard with Tesla and asset purchases of Tesla products.
High capital intensity and cash burn requiring large future fund raises, assumed primarily through debt.
Equity dilution from stock grants, management performance-based grants and potential equity raises.
Space: launch competition, higher internal allocation of launches, reliance on government contracts, FAA and other regulatory licenses, and fixed-price contract profitability.

Connectivity: broadband and mobile competition, reliance on Starship for launch capacity, scaling enterprise and government contracts, third-party distribution and spectrum partners, satellite licensing.
SI: unproven orbital datacenter compute, frontier AI model competition, scaling X advertising and X/Grok subscriptions, Starship dependence, and third-party chip supply such as NVDA GPUs.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 (GS estimates, many figures not confirmed by the company): SI Solutions & Infrastructure revenue of $24,659mm in 2026E, $150,103mm in 2027E and $238,770mm in 2028E. Year-end nameplate compute of 2,720MW in 2026E, 10,025MW in 2027E and 14,677MW in 2028E.
Exhibit 1 hosting deals: GS models Deal A at $15,000mm a year at $35 per MW, Google at $11,040mm a year at $45 per MW, Reflection AI at $1,800mm a year, and Deal C at $13,200mm a year.
Exhibit 4 SOTP: base-case 2029E EV of $3,869,778mm, discounted to $3,358,641mm, less $93,839mm net debt, on 13,250mm diluted shares for a $245 target. Downside value $110 and upside $330.
vol_and_positioning: Stock flows and trading dynamics from upcoming lock-up expirations are listed by GS as a driver of share performance in coming quarters.
SPCX trades about 25% below its peak post-IPO close. Market cap is $1.9tr and 3-month average daily traded value is $13.5bn.
Overhang risk: GS expects future capital raises (primarily debt) and possible equity dilution from stock grants to weigh on the shares until funding visibility improves.
